THE GENERAL BOARD
By
Andrew White
(Editorial from the August 19^7 issue of The Journal of Religious Education)
The first annual session of the General Board and the General Board of Education was held in Bethel A. M. E, Church, New York City on June 17, 18, 19, 1957. This session marked a departure into a new and better way of attending to the temporal business of the church. Heretofore, we had five or six different board meetings held at different times and in different sections of the country. Keeping up with the church meant keeping up with all of these boards and getting their printed annual reports.' With the advent of the General Board we get all the reports at one place and at one time. This permits the executives and others to get a clear telescopic view of the entire con-nectional program and to be intelligent about some of the details of each connectional agency of the church.
Who Are Members
The membership of the General Board is divided into two classes:
1.	Ex-officio membership and
2,	Voting membership
All active Bishops and General Officers and other officers receiving funds from the General Budget Fund are ex-officio members who have the right of the floor without the privilege of voting.
The voting membership of the Board is composed of two elders and two laymen from each Episcopal District, and nine elders and nine laymen at large. These members are elected by the General Conference upon nomination by the Bishops.
The General Board could probably be described as the fiscal agent of the A. M. E. Church. Its major sphere of concern is with our financial budget. It is charged with the responsibility of reviewing and approving or rejecting the operating budgets of all of the departments and agencies of the church, and administering all funds raised for the connectional operation of the i, M. E. Church. A careful reading of the 19^6 Discipline will enlighten you on all of the many financial details over which the General Board has final authority.
Beyond Finances
Even though our financial concerns are exceedingly important, it is far more important that we go beyond them into a far more vitally important area, that of Program Building. The only reason for being so concerned and careful about our finances is that we must have money in order to put over our program. Now since it is the major responsibility of the General Board to serve as the fiscal agent for the church, who then is responsible for Building Our Program? The immediate answer is that the Bishops and General Officers and other Connectional Officers are responsible for the Program Beyond Finance. Together they form the Program Committee of the A, M. E. Church while the General Board might be called the Finance Committee of the A. M. E, Church.
Each member of this Program Committee, meaning each Bishop, each General Officer, and each Connectional Officer, is definitely responsible for some specific phase of the Connectional Program. Collectively and individually they are duty-bound to successfully administer that phase of the connectional work committed to them. They are responsible for every detail involved in their overall program even though they themselves do not carry out every detail.
Since the Bishops and General Officers and other Connectional Officers are collectively and singularly responsible for the overall ponnectional program of our church, it would seem wise and would be very profitable if they would voluntarily form themselves into a Program Council. Through this informal council they could, after serious deliberation and hard work, give to our'denomination a unified overall Connectional program of Christian Education, Evangelism, and Missions. If this could be started now I feel certain that we would be able to go into the General Conference in I960 with a fairly detailed overall program for the A. M. E. Church.
I sincerely call upon the Bishops' Council to plan a retreat, asking each General Officer to come in and share in the initial steps involved in planning a unified overall connectional program for the A. M. E. Church. What do you think?"
